title: bug: a CLI that fails fast at launch (provider usage limit) makes the wrapper land and push a board-only checkpoint on every backoff retry
description: Measured by the governor on 2026-09-19. During a provider usage-limit window the CLI exits 1 within seconds of launch. The wrapper already classifies this ("CLI exits within 120s of launch (exit 1, 3 in a row) ... backing off up to 900s") but still runs a full post-flight landing on every retry. Each landing is a wip checkpoint whose only path is the task's own .moe/tasks/<id>.json (the claim touched the record), and it is pushed. Result: qa-7100be29 put 14 commits "wip(task-d1441364…) [status=REVIEW role=qa cli-exit=1]" on moe/work-2026-09-13 between 10:18Z and 12:36Z, and 46 cli-exit=1 checkpoint commits landed between 2026-09-18 20:00Z and 2026-09-19 12:50Z. None of them carries work, and they bury the real history. Board state is not lost by skipping them: the next real landing stages the task's BOARD path anyway. Proposed rule, identical in both twins: when an exit is classified as a launch failure and the landing would contain only BOARD paths, skip the checkpoint and log the skip. A launch-failure exit that has real (non-BOARD) dirty owned paths still lands as today.
definitionOfDone: A launch-failure exit whose landing would contain only the task's BOARD path lands no commit and logs a named skip, in both moe-agent.ps1 and moe-agent.sh
A launch-failure exit with a real owned code path still lands its checkpoint; a postflight arm per twin covers both cases and the skip arm fails on the old launchers
parity-check.{sh,ps1} pin the skip code; postflight.sh, postflight.ps1 (pwsh and PS 5.1) and both parity checks pass
reopenReason: Promoted by governor with the human's approval. Planning may proceed now; the WORKING claim stays gated on task-84150869 (both edit the launchers).
